newsitem.title: USA: Conn. heat wave sets record electricity demand.
newsitem.headline: Conn. heat wave sets record electricity demand.

text.p: The third straight day of sweltering, 90-degree Fahrenheit temperatures produced a record demand on the Connecticut power system Tuesday, a Northeast Utilities spokesman said.
"We set a new peak in Connecticut of 6,035 megawatts (MW), according to preliminary figures," Northeast spokesman Tom Shiel told Reuters.
The previous record of 5,635 MW was set on Monday, which erased the peak of 5,540 MW on July 21, 1994, Shiel said.

The figures measure combined usage by the state's three electricity suppliers: Northeast subsidiary Connecticut Light & Power, New Haven-based United Illuminating Co and the Connecticut Municipal Electric Energy Cooperative.
Shiel said that the Northeast Utilities system was holding up "very well" under the heat wave.
"So far, so good," he said. The utility did not have to implement any voltage reductions, and none are anticipated, he said.
"If the system continues to function as it has since the beginning of the summer, it looks good," Shiel said.
Shiel added that thunderstorms in Connecticut caused some 17,000 power outages on Tuesday afternoon, including about 12,400 in Manchester, Conn.
